subject: Post-demo: Deployment mode & Dedicated sizing follow-ups
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap & dedicated sizing asks

Hi Liam — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and a handful of follow-ups so we can size Dedicated correctly: 

1) Deployment preference: you said EdgeWorks prefers to keep inference in a customer-managed VPC but are open to trying Redwood Dedicated first if throughput/cost economics look compelling; please confirm whether Private VPC is a hard requirement or a future phase.

2) Workload profile (please confirm or correct):
   - Estimated steady-state requests: ~600 TPS during business hours (EMEA peak window)
   - Peak bursts: up to ~1,800 TPS for short periods (5-10 minutes)
   - Average response length: 220 tokens generated per request; typical prompt + response token mix ~300 tokens per call
   - Percent of calls that require context KV caching (session affinity): ~35%

3) Latency SLO: goal is P95 <= 220ms for single-request inference; P50 should be ~90–120ms.

4) GPU preference: you asked whether A100 vs H100 materially changes cost/SLA — Ben and Karthik will outline options, but to help us recommend a Dedicated SKU, can you confirm whether you prioritize lower latency (favor H100) vs lower per-token cost (A100 or quantized H100)?

Action items / next steps: 
- Liam: confirm whether Private VPC is required now vs later, and validate the TPS/token numbers above.
- Redwood (Ben/Karthik): provide a short sizing matrix (GPU type, node count, expected sustained TPS, expected token cost estimate) and a recommended canary plan (initial reserved pool + burst).

I attached the quick-capacity worksheet we use — fill any cells you want us to assume differently and drop it back. Also linking the demo recording where we showed prefix caching.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim

Thanks Rachel — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Deployment: Private VPC is preferred for our production rollout (data isolation and KMS integration). However, for a 6–8 week POC we are open to Redwood Dedicated if it can be deployed into our VPC or connected via a private peering arrangement.

- Traffic: the numbers look right. To be more explicit: steady-state 500–650 TPS (9–17:00 CET), with 2–3x spikes for marketing-driven events. We expect roughly 40% of calls to be multi-turn with KV cache relevance.

- Latency: P95 <= 300ms would be acceptable for initial rollout; long term we want ~200–220ms.

- GPU tradeoffs: cost is a constraint for us, but performance is critical for customer-facing features. If deduped quantized H100 or A100 options can keep P95 under 250–300ms at your recommended concurrency, that would be fine for the POC. For GA we would lean toward H100 if the price delta is justified.

We attached a short traffic export (small CSV) to the Drive folder — should help with token-mix estimates. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through it.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Product, EdgeWorks

Liam / Rachel — I put together a short sizing note based on the confirmed numbers: steady 600 TPS, 1.8k peak, avg 300 tokens per request, 40% multi-turn sessions. Key bullets: 

- Baseline recommendation (cost-conscious POC): 6 x A100-80GB nodes with a continuous batching configuration (target batch latency budget = 45ms). Estimated sustained throughput ~650 TPS at median latency ~120–160ms; P95 ~260–320ms depending on request distribution and cache hit rate. Expected effective token cost (hosted-style per-token equivalent) ~0.0042 USD/token when amortized across reserved capacity (rough calc).

- High-performance option (lower P95): 4 x H100-80GB nodes with agg-concurrency tuned + quantized kernels. Sustained throughput ~700 TPS, P95 ~170–230ms, better headroom for bursts. Token cost estimate ~0.0054 USD/token (higher hardware premium).

- Concurrency + KV caching: with 40% multi-turn, enabling session locality and KV cache reduces compute by ~18–25% for those sessions. We recommend a mix: reserve capacity for steady 600 TPS and configure burst pool to scale to additional 1,200 TPS for 15-minute windows.

- Canary plan: start with 4 nodes (A100) as a conservative reserved pool and run production traffic ramp for 2 weeks; monitor P95 and cost. If P95/P50 drift high, upgrade to H100 or add nodes.

Attachments: short capacity matrix (I pasted the key rows into the Drive link).

- Ben

Following up with a quick concurrency and token-mix model to help EdgeWorks pick a starting point. I used the numbers provided and ran two scenarios: "cost-first" (A100 baseline) and "latency-first" (H100 with quantization). Highlights below: 

- Assumptions: average request 300 tokens, generation ratio 0.73, effective batch size target 32 for steady-state.

- Cost-first (A100): to reliably hit 600 TPS sustained, plan for 6 nodes @ target concurrency 4–6 per GPU instance, with dynamic batching and a short-lived burst pool for marketing spikes. Expected P95 ~250–320ms; if you enable prefix caching aggressively (we can rollout session affinity rules), you should see 12–20% token/cost reduction over time.

- Latency-first (H100): 4 nodes, higher single-query throughput and lower P95 (~160–220ms). Requires tighter kernel tuning (we can handle this), and quantization to 4/8-bit will save cost while keeping latency benefits.

Practical recommendation: For EdgeWorks' POC, run A100 reserved pool (4 nodes) + 2 node burst reservation (A100) and a test H100 configuration behind a canary route in parallel. That lets you validate the H100 latency gains and pick GA path after 2 weeks of traffic.

Next steps I suggest we do a 45-minute technical deep-dive with your infra team to talk VPC peering/private connectivity options and confirm KMS/HSM workflow. Proposed times: Tue 8/18 10:00 CET or Wed 8/19 15:00 CET.

— Karthik
